artifacts.description: feat(kernel): split the faces of a body by a plane (M6-02b)

acceptance_criteria: `fn split_faces(&self, s: &Self::Shape, plane: &Workplane) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>`, documented: `s` with every face that the infinite plane through `plane.origin` with normal `plane.normal` crosses divided along the intersection (`x_dir` unused). The geometry is unchanged: same solids, volume and surface area. A plane that crosses no face, or only touches the shape along an existing face or edge, returns a shape with the same face count. `s` is unchanged.
A non-finite origin, or a zero or non-finite normal, is `InvalidInput`, checked by the plain function `prepare_split` before the backend (already unit-tested; add no duplicate).

With `--features occt` (1e-9 relative on volumes and areas, exact on counts): 1. Box 10 × 5 × 2 at the origin, plane x = 4 (normal +X): 1 body, volume 100, surface area 160, 10 faces, 20 edges, 12 vertices (`sub_shape_count`). 2. The same box and the plane x = 20: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices, volume 100. 3. The same box and the plane z = 0 (its bottom face): 6 faces, volume 100. 4. Cylinder of radius 5 and height 10, base centered at the origin, axis +Z, split by the plane y = 0 (normal +Y): 1 body, volume 250π, surface area 150π, more faces than the unsplit cylinder (state both counts in the test), and every face's bounding box (`sub_shape_bounding_box`) lies within y ≤ 1e-6 or y ≥ −1e-6 (no face crosses the plane). 5. A zero normal returns `InvalidInput` through `OcctKernel`, and the input's face count is unchanged after a successful split.
Every `unsafe` block added in `swx-kernel::ffi` is documented; the shim function is `noexcept` and catches all C++ exceptions (ADR 2026-10-13).
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and CI's `swx-kernel (occt)` job passes.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
